item.title: Binary Mitigation Challenge
item.description: Since ASLR is active, memory addresses are not consistent I am learning how to bypass binary exploitation mitigations. These are my notes about an exercise I solved. Initial analysis The provided program reads two inputs and prints them on stdout. Then, it continuously rereads the second input and prints both buffers on stdout. item.title: H4cked writeup
item.description: H4cked - TryHackMe Room walkthrough [H4cked]https://tryhackme.com/room/h4cked is a beginner room from TryHackMe. We’ll have to apply offensive and defensive concepts to complete the room. Oh no! We’ve been hacked! We begin by reading that some intruder has found his way into one of our machines, and the .pcapng is our forensic evidence. We can start by opening the file in Wireshark to analyze its content. Immediately, we see that the attacker has tried, successfully, to brute force our host through the FTP service on port 21:
